rule_name: G6PD deficiency - oxidant drug hemolysis risk
indian_frequency_claim: 2-27.9% carrier prevalence depending on region/community (highest: Vataliya Prajapati Gujarat 27.9% males; tribal Odisha/Central India 6-8%; general population survey 1.9%; lowest in some North Indian cohorts <1%)
observability_rationale: Acute haemolysis (dark urine, jaundice, fatigue) days after starting primaquine/dapsone is a well-documented, recognizable clinical pattern; weaker for nitrofurantoin/co-trimoxazole (rare reports despite wide use per CPIC).
opd_actionability_rationale: Dispensed at PHC/OPD level (malaria elimination programme, NLEP, routine antibiotics); point-of-care G6PD test or referral before dosing is an OPD-level action.

indian_frequency_claim: CYP2C19*2 allele frequency 0.34-0.36 (IndiGen national + South Indian CAD cohorts); GenomeIndia national poor-metabolizer phenotype ~15%
indian_frequency_sources: PMID:35338580 (IndiGen, *2 AF=0.36); PMID:41028360 (South Indian CAD/clopidogrel cohort, 34% PM/IM carriers); PMID:37985132 (South Indian ACS cohort); medRxiv:10.64898/2026.03.20.26348801 (GenomeIndia, 15% PM phenotype)
observability_rationale: Recurrent stent thrombosis, recurrent ACS, or stroke on clopidogrel despite adherence is a strong, well-recognized signal of poor-metabolizer status.
opd_actionability_rationale: Switching to prasugrel/ticagrelor or adding antiplatelet therapy is routine cardiology/OPD follow-up decision-making; genotyping increasingly available via referral.

indian_frequency_claim: VKORC1 -1639G>A AF 0.14-0.72 depending on region (IGVdb range 6.5%->70% across 24 subpopulations); CYP2C9*3 AF 0.09-0.17 (higher in North Indian anticoagulant cohorts)
indian_frequency_sources: PMID:35338580 (IndiGen, VKORC1 AF=0.18); PMID:25155935 (IGVdb, 24 subpopulations, VKORC1 range 6.5-70%); PMID:23563037 (North vs South Indian pilot); PMID:26781925 (North Indian valve-replacement cohort on acenocoumarol)
observability_rationale: Excessive INR/bleeding at low dose, or persistent sub-therapeutic INR at high dose, is a directly observable signal via routine INR monitoring already standard of care.
opd_actionability_rationale: Dose titration via INR monitoring is routine OPD/anticoagulation-clinic practice; no new infrastructure needed.

indian_frequency_claim: NUDT15*3 AF 0.068-0.107 in Indian thiopurine-treated cohorts (up to 20.8% in some Austro-Asiatic tribal groups); TPMT variants comparatively rare in India (*3C AF 0.02, *3A AF 0.003) -- NUDT15 is the dominant thiopurine-toxicity gene in South Asians, not TPMT
indian_frequency_sources: PMID:35338580 (IndiGen NUDT15*3=0.08, TPMT*3A/*3C); PMID:29470173 (Indian thiopurine cohort, NUDT15*3=0.107); PMID:32935219 (Indian GSA screening N=2000); medRxiv:10.64898/2026.03.20.26348801 (GenomeIndia tribal groups)
observability_rationale: Cytopenia (leukopenia) on routine follow-up CBC while on thiopurine therapy is a moderately specific signal, though confounded by disease activity and other marrow suppressants.
opd_actionability_rationale: Dose reduction or alternative agent is an OPD-level decision once myelosuppression is flagged on routine CBC monitoring.

indian_frequency_claim: CYP2D6 poor/intermediate-metabolizer alleles (*4, *10, *41) 6.6-32% depending on allele/region; CYP2C19*2 AF 0.36 nationally
indian_frequency_sources: PMID:35338580 (IndiGen); PMID:12942225 (South Indian Tamilian cohort); PMID:16880622 (South Indian states); PMID:31368850 (South Indian resequencing cohort)
observability_rationale: Excess sedation/anticholinergic side effects (possible PM) vs. non-response at standard dose (possible UM) is a moderately usable signal on OPD follow-up, though confounded by other factors.
opd_actionability_rationale: Dose titration for TCAs in OPD psychiatry/pain/neuropathy management is routine practice.

indian_frequency_claim: Same CYP2D6 PM/IM allele burden as above (6.6-32%)
observability_rationale: Side-effect profile is nonspecific; atomoxetine use in Indian OPD/psychiatry is moderate but growing, behind stimulants -- weaker standalone signal.
opd_actionability_rationale: Dose adjustment is possible at OPD/psychiatry follow-up level.

indian_frequency_claim: Same CYP2D6 PM/IM/UM allele burden as above
observability_rationale: Poor analgesia (PM) or sedation/toxicity (UM) is observable but codeine use has declined in Indian OPD due to abuse-potential restrictions, reducing exposure and signal frequency.
opd_actionability_rationale: Alternative analgesic can be chosen at OPD level.

rule_name: CYP2C19 - proton pump inhibitor metabolizer variability
observability_rationale: Poor symptom control at standard PPI dose could reflect ultrarapid metabolizer status, but is heavily confounded by H. pylori status, adherence, and lifestyle -- weak standalone signal.
opd_actionability_rationale: Dose/drug switch (e.g. to a non-CYP2C19-dependent option) is a routine OPD decision for reflux/PUD.

rule_name: HLA-B*15:02 / HLA-A*31:01 - carbamazepine severe cutaneous reaction risk
indian_frequency_claim: HLA-B*15:02 ~3% carrier prevalence (IndiGen); strong disease association in Indian case-control studies (OR up to 38.5); HLA-A*31:01 ~2% carrier prevalence (IndiGen)
indian_frequency_sources: PMID:35338580 (IndiGen); PMID:25266342 (meta-analysis, Malaysian-Indian + India-pooled, OR 38.54); PMID:25305458 (North Indian case-control); PMID:29076187 (Kerala case-control)
observability_rationale: SJS/TEN is a severe, recognizable ADR, but by the time it is observed, harm has already occurred -- this is a pre-emptive flag, not a post-hoc one.
opd_actionability_rationale: Pre-prescription HLA-B*15:02 screening exists but is not routinely ordered in Indian OPD; if unavailable, doctor can choose an alternative anticonvulsant empirically, especially with prior history.

rule_name: NAT2 slow acetylator - isoniazid hepatotoxicity risk
indian_frequency_claim: Slow-acetylator phenotype 44-74% depending on region (Mumbai 55%, North India 44-53%, South India 67-74%; Chennai TB cohort 58% slow)
indian_frequency_sources: PMID:28862181 / PMC5460557 (IJMR, Chennai NAT2 genotyping); Dovepress review 'NAT2 Acetylation Phenotypes in India'
observability_rationale: Hepatotoxicity (deranged LFTs) or peripheral neuropathy on isoniazid is a recognizable, commonly monitored OPD/NTEP signal.
opd_actionability_rationale: Isoniazid dosing is standardized under NTEP weight-band protocols, but LFT monitoring and drug switch/interruption on hepatotoxicity is an OPD-level decision.

rule_name: CYP2D6 poor metabolizer - tamoxifen reduced efficacy
indian_frequency_claim: Same CYP2D6 PM/IM allele burden as above (6.6-32%)
observability_rationale: Breast cancer recurrence on tamoxifen is a delayed, highly confounded signal, and management is oncology-led, not primary-care.
opd_actionability_rationale: Dosing/switch decisions are typically managed in oncology, not general OPD.

rule_name: CYP2C19 poor metabolizer - voriconazole toxicity risk
observability_rationale: Sub-therapeutic levels (PM) or visual/hepatic toxicity (UM) require drug-level monitoring rarely available in OPD; antifungal dosing for invasive infections is typically hospital/ID-specialist managed.
opd_actionability_rationale: Dosing decisions typically happen in hospital/ID-specialist setting, not general OPD.

rule_name: CYP3A5 expresser status - tacrolimus dose requirement
indian_frequency_claim: GenomeIndia Tibeto-Burman group poor-metabolizer (non-expresser) phenotype 45%; broader pan-India CYP3A5*3 frequency not established in this search
data_quality: NO_INDIAN_DATA — closest proxy: GenomeIndia Tibeto-Burman subgroup only, not representative of pan-India frequency
observability_rationale: Sub-therapeutic tacrolimus levels are only detectable via specialist drug-level monitoring, not general OPD observation.
opd_actionability_rationale: Transplant immunosuppression dosing is managed by transplant specialists, not general OPD.

indian_frequency_claim: UGT1A1*28 allele frequency in Indians is comparable to other Asian populations and notably higher than East Asians at some related loci; Balram et al. 2002 (Singapore-based Indian ethnic cohort) found UGT1A1*28 to be a common allele in Indians. A separate South Indian healthy-cohort study (N=450-608) found UGT1A1 (TA)7 promoter allele frequency 39.8%.
indian_frequency_sources: PMID:11773869 (Balram et al. 2002, Pharmacogenetics -- Indian ethnic cohort, Singapore); South Indian healthy cohort TPMT/UGT1A1/MDR1 study (N=450-608, ResearchGate abstract, PMID not captured in this pass -- flagged for follow-up)
observability_rationale: Jaundice/hyperbilirubinemia (atazanavir) or severe neutropenia/diarrhea (irinotecan) are fairly specific, specialist-monitored signals.
opd_actionability_rationale: ART regimen switch happens within NACO ART centres; chemotherapy dosing is oncology-managed -- not general OPD decisions, but flag is useful for referral communication.

indian_frequency_sources: NO_INDIAN_DATA — closest proxy: pooled Asian meta-analysis (source not independently confirmed as covering India), South/West Asian gnomAD range 5-10% per CPIC guideline text
